name: Intent and request intake
definition: Turn a request into a structured work item with a clear purpose and completion criteria.
acceptance: Given an ambiguous request, capture missing information before work is routed.

name: Human approval experience
definition: Let an authorised person inspect the proposed action, evidence and consequences.
acceptance: Record approver, scope and expiry; reject a stale or unauthorised approval.

name: Progress and feedback
definition: Expose work status and capture corrections without losing task context.
acceptance: A user can find the current state, submit a correction and see who owns the next step.

name: Accessible channels
definition: Support the channels and accessibility needs of each audience.
acceptance: The same work item retains identity and permissions when moving between supported channels.

name: Work classification
definition: Assess task complexity, risk and reversibility before selecting an execution mode.
acceptance: A high-impact action cannot inherit the routing of a low-risk information request.

name: Planning and routing
definition: Allocate work among people, deterministic workflows, automations and agents.
acceptance: Record why a route was selected and what happens when its executor is unavailable.

name: Autonomy policy
definition: Set permitted actions and approval gates for each use case.
acceptance: A policy change or revocation is enforced before the next consequential action.

name: Durable workflows
definition: Resume work safely across failures, waits and deployments.
acceptance: Restart during an approval wait without losing state or repeating a completed side effect.

name: Tool gateway
definition: Authorise and audit access to enterprise tools.
acceptance: Reject an unapproved tool or excessive scope, even when requested by a valid agent.

name: Human execution
definition: Support a person completing work with context and clear accountability.
acceptance: A human receives the evidence, due date and permitted actions needed to finish the assigned task.

name: Deterministic automation
definition: Execute repeatable rules with explicit inputs, outputs and failure paths.
acceptance: Replaying the same event cannot apply the same business transaction twice.

name: Agent execution
definition: Carry out bounded reasoning and tool use against task completion criteria.
acceptance: Stop on budget, permission or quality limits and return a recoverable task state.

name: Domain packs
definition: Package domain workflows, vocabularies and tests on shared platform services.
acceptance: A domain configuration can change without forking common runtime or control logic.

name: Process analysis
definition: Find delays, rework and exceptions using evidence from actual work.
acceptance: Separate a genuine process bottleneck from a missing or duplicated event.

name: Evaluation and feedback
definition: Measure quality using representative cases and production feedback.
acceptance: A proposed change must pass a held-out evaluation and a regression comparison.

name: Controlled improvement
definition: Test and release changes with measurable success and rollback criteria.
acceptance: Compare the baseline with the changed process and roll back when guardrail metrics deteriorate.

name: Knowledge improvement
definition: Turn corrections and recurring failures into reviewed knowledge updates.
acceptance: A corrected answer creates a traceable review item instead of silently rewriting a source.

name: Service observability
definition: Trace a business request across orchestration, execution and supporting systems.
acceptance: Locate the failed dependency from a user-visible work identifier.

name: Value and cost monitoring
definition: Connect operating costs and performance to business outcomes.
acceptance: Report cost per accepted outcome including model, infrastructure and human review costs.

name: Assurance evidence
definition: Retain evidence of decisions, controls and exceptions.
acceptance: An assessor can reconstruct who authorised an action and which policy applied.

name: Portfolio governance
definition: Track ownership, lifecycle and dependencies across AI-enabled services.
acceptance: Every production use case has an accountable owner, review date and retirement plan.

name: Grounded retrieval
definition: Retrieve relevant evidence within the requester’s permissions.
acceptance: An answer cites accessible sources and does not reveal content outside the user’s entitlement.

name: Knowledge lifecycle
definition: Manage provenance, freshness, review and retirement of reusable knowledge.
acceptance: An expired source is visibly flagged and cannot silently remain authoritative.

name: Memory scopes
definition: Separate working, session, user and case memory with explicit retention.
acceptance: A deletion request removes applicable memory without exposing another user’s or tenant’s context.

name: Ontology and semantics
definition: Define shared business terms and their domain extensions.
acceptance: Two systems using different names for one entity can be mapped with an explicit owner and version.

name: Identity and delegated authority
definition: Identify actors and limit their authority for each action.
acceptance: An agent cannot reuse another actor’s privileges or continue after delegation expires.

name: Policy and guardrails
definition: Enforce allowed data use, outputs and business actions.
acceptance: An adversarial document cannot change the tool permissions or approval rules.

name: Safety and assurance
definition: Assess failure modes and verify control effectiveness over time.
acceptance: Test known misuse cases and route unexplained control failures to an accountable owner.

name: Privacy and isolation
definition: Apply minimisation, retention and isolation to data and context.
acceptance: Cross-tenant access and prohibited retention are rejected and recorded.

name: Roles and accountability
definition: Assign responsibility for outcomes, oversight and exceptions.
acceptance: An exception always has a named role able to intervene and a clear escalation path.

name: Skills and adoption
definition: Develop practical competence and support changes in work.
acceptance: Practitioners demonstrate a recovery task before supervising the corresponding automation.

name: Oversight capacity
definition: Keep human review effective at the expected workload.
acceptance: Measure approval load and response time; reduce automation when review capacity is exhausted.

name: Operating and commercial model
definition: Align teams, service boundaries and incentives with delivered value.
acceptance: A service agreement states ownership and cost allocation for human and automated work.

name: Agent harness
definition: Coordinate the reasoning loop, tools, stopping conditions and recovery within an agent run.
acceptance: A run observes budgets and allowed tools, checkpoints progress and stops safely on repeated failure.

name: LLM kernel and model abstraction
definition: Provide a consistent contract for model calls and structured responses.
acceptance: A model replacement preserves output contracts and surfaces capability differences explicitly.

name: Inference and model serving
definition: Serve model requests within latency, throughput and cost targets.
acceptance: Load and failure tests demonstrate bounded queueing, fallback and budget enforcement.

name: Context engineering
definition: Assemble task instructions, retrieved evidence and memory within context limits.
acceptance: When context is compacted, permissions and unresolved task commitments remain intact.

name: Model and prompt lifecycle
definition: Version, evaluate and release model configurations, prompts and adapters.
acceptance: A release can be traced to evaluation results and rolled back to a known configuration.

name: AI platform operations
definition: Operate shared evaluation, tracing, secrets and deployment services.
acceptance: An incident can be isolated to a runtime or model version without losing the business work record.

name: Process digitisation
definition: Represent business steps, decisions and records in operational systems.
acceptance: A selected process has a digital work identifier, owner, state transitions and exception path.

name: Enterprise systems of record
definition: Maintain authoritative ERP, CRM, ITSM and other business records.
acceptance: Define which system owns each entity and how corrections propagate without conflicting masters.

name: Digital customer and employee channels
definition: Capture interactions and hand them into executable business processes.
acceptance: A channel interaction becomes a traceable work item with consent and identity context.

name: Integration and events
definition: Expose governed APIs and events for reading and changing business state.
acceptance: Duplicate or out-of-order events cannot silently corrupt a business record.

name: Data products and quality
definition: Provide owned, documented operational and analytical data with quality contracts.
acceptance: Consumers can identify freshness, lineage, access rules and an owner for a broken contract.

name: Digital infrastructure
definition: Provide the hosting, connectivity and recovery foundations for digital operations.
acceptance: A recovery exercise restores a priority business process within its agreed recovery targets.
